frozen_target.question: After the unique nonsquare decomposition n=D t^2 linearizes the phase on each squarefree radical channel, can the nonexact channels of the literal hard-TOP coefficient be coupled at one arbitrary fixed real centre before every absolute value to save L^(1/2-o(1)), or do the varying B_D(t) vectors, modulo-one square-root collisions, factorization norms, source hypotheses, or restored powers repay the entire gain?
frozen_target.reference_formula: T_L^ns=sum_(D>1 squarefree) sum_(t>=1) B_D(t)e(t J sqrt(D)), where B_D(t)=L^(3/2)(D t^2)^(-3/4) C_L(D t^2)1_(D t^2 asymp L^2), and C_L is the exact odd upper-near-square truncated chi4 divisor coefficient with eta_L, Phi, W, q_X, floors, parity, hard entries/exits, and zero extension retained. The target is |T_L^ns| <<_epsilon L^(3/2)X^epsilon.
quantities: J=sqrt(X), y=floor(J), q_X=X/y^2, H=floor(y X^(-1/4)), and 1<<L<<H is one half-open polynomial intermediate block.
For hm=D t^2, the unique incidence coordinates are h=g d1 u^2, m=g d2 v^2, d1 d2=D, t=g u v, (d1 u,d2 v)=1, d2 v^2<=d1 u^2<=4 d2 v^2, with g,d1,u odd.
Accepted controls are sum_n |C_L(n)|^2 << L^2 log(2L) and sum_t |B_D(t)| <<_epsilon (1+L/sqrt(D))L^epsilon.
The positive capacity is L^(2+o(1)); the target needs L^(1/2-o(1)) genuine signed gain.
At one fixed centre at most one whole D-channel is phase one and it is target-safe; no near-resonance conclusion is accepted.
Any common-test theorem must first prove and price a literal decomposition of the D-dependent vectors B_D(t).
No conclusion transfers outside this one nonsquare polynomial intermediate hard-TOP block.

closing_assessment.main_result: The exact radical-incidence dictionary removes every fixed-constant long channel D<=CL and classifies all exact base and atom collisions. The mandatory t=1,D asymptotic to L^2 face has one-column common-test capacity L^(2+o(1)); coefficient-uniform projective placement and the four audited primary-source interfaces do not supply the missing L^(1/2-o(1)).
